purpose: P1 method intelligence for AffectiveArt Track1. P0 public EmoArt data is already local; these cards identify public methods from organizers/collaborators or closely related resources that can be converted into Track1 FID/AAS optimization modules.
non_goals: Do not use private test labels.
Do not mutate the current champion package.
Do not treat public EmoArt rows as hidden-test gold.
Do not claim a method improves official score until validated by local gates and official submission feedback.

cards.source_group: Cheng Zhang / Hongxia Xie / Wen-Huang Cheng
cards.core_method: Attribute-Grounded Selective Reasoning: five attribute-specific agents decide whether color, composition, line, light, and brushstroke are emotionally salient before a final agent reasons over the selected cues.
cards.track1_transfer: Use the same salience bottleneck to stop prompt packets and AAS judges from mechanically listing all five attributes. For each Track1 sample, select 2-3 operative visual levers that should control generation and evaluation.
cards.expected_gain: Higher AAS stability with less prompt bloat; lower risk that reference-guided prompts over-constrain every image into the same template.
risks: FAB-G targets Track2-style understanding, not image generation.
Training the six Qwen3-VL LoRA adapters may be too slow for final Track1 submissions.
Use AGSR-lite schema first; only train LoRA if time and GPU budget allow.
cards.first_experiment: Build an AGSR-lite cue selector over current Track1 captions and official reference annotations; compare generated prompt length, attribute diversity, and human AAS risk on 50 samples.

cards.source_group: Hongxia Xie / Hong-Han Shuai / Wen-Huang Cheng
cards.core_method: Emotion visual instruction tuning: build emotion-specific instruction data so a VLM predicts emotion and explains visual evidence rather than only generic caption content.
cards.track1_transfer: Use emotion-instruction templates as a candidate review and prompt-critique layer. The generator prompt should specify visual cues that convey the target affect, not only objects and style words.
cards.expected_gain: Better separation between caption object fidelity and emotion-aware visual expression; useful for AAS attribute alignment and Track2 description consistency.
risks: EmoVIT is an understanding model family, not a Gemini image-generation controller.
A VLM judge can be anchored by the caption; blind image-first review is still required.
cards.first_experiment: Create a Gemini/EmoVIT-style review prompt that asks for image-first affective evidence, then compare against current VLM gate on known relation/style failures.

cards.core_method: PromptFix uses VLM understanding and an auxiliary prompt adapter to repair real-world images without manually writing a bespoke prompt for each case.
cards.track1_transfer: Convert weak Track1 candidates into repair prompts: detect missing/incorrect objects, physical logic errors, visible text artifacts, or template overfit, then generate a targeted repair prompt rather than regenerating blindly.
cards.expected_gain: Higher yield from expensive Gemini generations; fewer reruns for hands/glass, flags/ropes, relation logic, landmark, and poster-layout problems.
risks: PromptFix is an image restoration/editing pipeline; Gemini image API may not expose the same control surface.
Repair prompts can overfit local errors and degrade FID if they become too literal.
cards.first_experiment: Run a 20-sample repair queue from known visual failures and compare current one-shot regeneration vs repair-prompt regeneration.

cards.source_group: Sicheng Zhao visual emotion analysis lineage
cards.core_method: Affective Image Content Analysis survey: highlights affective gap, subjectivity, domain adaptation, label distribution learning, and affective region/entity reasoning.
cards.track1_transfer: Treat Track1 generation as a multi-objective affective distribution problem, not a deterministic caption-to-image problem. Route samples by emotion/style family and preserve distribution diversity.
cards.expected_gain: Lower FID overfit to high-contrast posters; better coverage of low-arousal positive painterly distribution seen in EmoArt.
risks: Survey methods are not turnkey code.
Emotion distribution priors can hurt AAS if they override explicit caption content.
cards.first_experiment: Add emotion/style-family buckets to candidate selection and verify whether B80/B120/B160 replacements preserve or improve public EmoArt distribution coverage.

cards.core_method: The challenge proposal and EmoArt benchmark expose a style-adaptation baseline direction: style examples, LoRA-style adaptation, and AAS based on generated attribute descriptions.
cards.track1_transfer: Because final generation uses Gemini, we cannot directly train LoRA inside Gemini. Instead, emulate the baseline upstream: retrieve style-family references, select style-specific prompt packets, and gate candidates against style-family proxy.
cards.expected_gain: Directly targets the official FID gap by aligning generated image batches to the public EmoArt style distribution.
risks: OpenReview proposal may differ from final Codabench scoring.
Over-retrieval can make all samples look like copied reference boards.
cards.first_experiment: Expand each sample from top4 references to a 20-50 item style family profile and score candidate distance to that family before package selection.

cards.source_group: Ling Lo / Hong-Han Shuai / Wen-Huang Cheng affective relation lineage
cards.core_method: Micro-expression recognition work uses relation/graph reasoning over subtle facial or temporal cues; related surveys emphasize subtle cue localization and robustness.
cards.track1_transfer: The direct domain is different, but the idea transfers to relation semantics: objects being present is not enough; their spatial/causal relation must match the caption.
cards.expected_gain: Better detection of failures like soldiers chasing civilians instead of protecting them, hands crossing glass, or flags attached unrealistically.
risks: Micro-expression datasets are not artwork-generation data.
This should guide gate design, not model training for Track1.
cards.first_experiment: Represent hard captions as subject-action-object relation triples and require blind image review to verify relation polarity.

cards.core_method: EmoArt code includes CLIP score, attribute alignment, lexical diversity metrics such as TTR/MTLD, and entropy-style text diversity tools.
cards.track1_transfer: Use these metrics as local proxy components for candidate prompts and image descriptions: penalize repeated template prompts, overlong attribute flooding, and text-like visual artifacts.
cards.expected_gain: Reduces template collapse in both prompts and generated images; supports stronger package-level candidate selection.
risks: Metric code was designed for dataset evaluation, not official hidden Track1 scoring.
Text diversity alone can reward irrelevant verbosity if not tied to image evidence.
cards.first_experiment: Score v3, B80, B120, B160 prompts and candidates for template repetition and correlate with human review outcomes.

cards.core_method: EmoVerse provides body-action-scene triplets, concise/detailed emotion descriptions, and grounded object evidence using detection/segmentation pipelines.
cards.track1_transfer: Use a similar body-action-scene decomposition for hard Track1 captions before generation and review, especially propaganda, battlefield, train, crowd, and object-interaction scenes.
cards.expected_gain: Stronger content planning and relation consistency before image generation.
risks: Dataset emotion ontology does not match AffectiveArt 12 classes.
External grounding pipeline may add complexity without direct FID gain.
cards.first_experiment: Add body-action-scene fields to prompt packets for 50 high-risk narrative samples and compare relation error rate.

cards.core_method: Quality assessment and perceptual multimedia evaluation lineage; useful as a signal that image realism, artifact detection, and perceptual quality matter alongside semantic alignment.
cards.track1_transfer: Add visual artifact and perceptual-quality features to candidate gates, especially for distorted anatomy, fake text, compressed/card-like images, and provider placeholder artifacts.
cards.expected_gain: Stops candidates that pass caption review but damage FID/perceptual distribution.
risks: Need stronger primary-source mapping to specific Sanghoon Lee Track1-relevant algorithms before claiming direct transfer.
Quality metrics can prefer photorealism over painterly artwork if not style-conditioned.
cards.first_experiment: Keep as a watch card; implement only style-conditioned artifact checks already supported by current review images.

cards.source_group: Hongxia Xie / Bin Wen / Ruoxuan Zhang generation-data lineage
cards.core_method: AVC Lab research page lists structured multimodal generation projects such as CookAnything and MindPower, suggesting a broader strategy of data-rich multi-stage generation rather than one-shot prompting.
cards.track1_transfer: Keep the pipeline multi-stage: plan -> retrieve -> generate -> blind review -> repair -> package select. This validates our current direction but is not a direct code drop.
cards.expected_gain: Better process discipline and fewer single-shot failures.
risks: First pass found project-level signals, not enough primary algorithm detail for Track1 implementation.
Do not overfit unrelated cooking/mental-health generation tasks.
cards.first_experiment: Use this only as architectural support while prioritizing FAB-G, EmoVIT, AICA, and PromptFix cards.
